# Inkstone

> A native Markdown notes app for macOS 26 and iOS 26. Plain Markdown files in a
> folder you choose — no database, no proprietary format, no account, no
> Electron. Reads and writes the same vaults Obsidian does.

Inkstone is free. Its source is public at https://github.com/iamzifei/inkstone
but carries no open-source licence, so the accurate description is
source-available rather than open source.

Three decisions the rest follows from:

- **The files are the truth.** No database and no import step. A vault Obsidian
  created opens in Inkstone and vice versa. App state lives in a hidden
  `.inkstone` folder you are free to delete.
- **A broken link is permanent.** With no database to repair one, renaming a note
  rewrites every wikilink pointing at it across the whole vault, in the same
  action.
- **The engine knows nothing about screens.** Parsing, indexing, search and the
  graph live in a Swift package that imports no UI framework, so they are covered
  by real tests rather than a simulator.

## What it does

- Live preview editing — syntax renders in place and is revealed on the line the
  cursor is on. Source and reading modes as well.
- Wikilinks, embeds, block references, aliases in frontmatter, backlinks, and
  unresolved-link tracking.
- Frontmatter shown as a properties table at the top of the note.
- Graph view of the whole vault or one note's neighbourhood, with filters, colour
  groups and force controls.
- Canvas in the open JSON Canvas 1.0 format.
- Tags inline or in frontmatter, nested, in any script. Fuzzy quick switcher and
  full-text search with `tag:` and `path:` operators.
- Math, Mermaid diagrams, transclusion, image and PDF embeds.
- Daily notes, a calendar, bookmarks, version history, split view.
- Typography built for setting Chinese and English on one line: hair spacing at
  the CJK–Latin boundary, punctuation compression, independent body and code
  fonts.
- Sync through iCloud, or through a GitHub repository you own — including on
  iPhone and iPad, via the GitHub Contents API rather than libgit2.

## What it does not do

- No plugin API. Obsidian's plugin ecosystem has no equivalent here.
- macOS and iOS only. No Windows, Linux or Android build.
- No published-site feature equivalent to Obsidian Publish.

## Pages

- [Home](https://inkslab.app/): what the app is, with a screen recording.
- [Obsidian alternative](https://inkslab.app/obsidian-alternative.html): an
  honest comparison, including what Inkstone does not have.
- [Syncing a vault for free](https://inkslab.app/obsidian-sync-free.html): what
  Obsidian Sync costs, the free routes, and where each one breaks.
- [Sync guide](https://inkslab.app/sync.html): setting up GitHub sync across two
  devices.
- [Privacy](https://inkslab.app/privacy.html): nothing is collected. No account,
  no analytics, no server of ours.
- [Source](https://github.com/iamzifei/inkstone)
- [Releases](https://github.com/iamzifei/inkstone/releases/latest)

## Requirements

macOS 26 or iOS 26, Apple silicon. Interface in English, 简体中文 and 繁體中文.
